extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and patent practitioners (U.S. attorneys/agents) preparing and prosecuting U.S. patent applications before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_short: application data sheet and correspondence rules
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality/formatting requirements for specifying and changing the correspondence address, providing contact/bibliographic data via an Application Data Sheet (ADS), and resolving inconsistencies among ADS and other application papers in U.S. patent filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address mandatory specification (37 CFR 1.33(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must specify a correspondence address to which the Office will send notices, letters, and other communications relating to an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The correspondence address must either be in an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76) or be set forth in a clearly identifiable manner elsewhere in any papers submitted with the application filing. If no correspondence address is specified, the Office may treat the mailing address of the first named inventor as the correspondence address (when provided). The Office will generally not engage in double correspondence except as deemed necessary by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where correspondence address appears (priority among documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple correspondence addresses are specified or conflict, the Office will select one address for use and follows an explicit priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than one correspondence address is specified in a single document the Office will select one; where different papers direct non-matching addresses, priority is accorded in this order: (A) Application Data Sheet (ADS); (B) application transmittal; (C) oath or declaration (unless power of attorney is more current); and (D) power of attorney. The ADS is often the most recently created document and is preferred by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for Customer Number address over typed address
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple addresses are given, the Office will select an address associated with a Customer Number over a typed correspondence address, if given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than one correspondence address is specified in a single document, and one is associated with a Customer Number and another is a typed address, Office will select the Customer Number-associated address for use as the correspondence address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daytime telephone number requested for correspondence party
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a daytime telephone number of the party to whom correspondence is to be addressed is requested pursuant to 37 CFR 1.33(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While business is conducted on the written record, a daytime telephone number is useful for initiating contact that can later be reduced to writing. Any party who could change the correspondence address could also change the telephone number. The telephone number should be supplied in a clearly identifiable manner and may be changed by any party who may change the correspondence address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may change correspondence address before filing oath/declaration (37 CFR 1.33(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to filing an executed oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 by any inventor, who may change the correspondence address is specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no § 1.63 oath or declaration has been filed, the correspondence address may be changed by the party who filed the application. If filed by a patent practitioner, any other patent practitioner named in the transmittal papers may also change the correspondence address. Thus inventor(s), any patent practitioner named in the transmittal papers, or a filing assignee may change the correspondence address under this paragraph. A patent practitioner named only on letterhead is not considered 'named in the transmittal papers' for this purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may change correspondence address after filing oath/declaration (37 CFR 1.33(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an executed oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 has been filed by any inventor, the parties who may change the correspondence address are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 37 CFR 1.33(a)(2) the correspondence address may be changed by (A) a patent practitioner of record, (B) an assignee as provided under 37 CFR 3.71(b), or (C) all of the applicants (37 CFR 1.41(b)) for patent, unless there is an assignee of the entire interest and such assignee has taken action in accordance with 37 CFR 3.71.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and notice requirements for a change of correspondence address
rubrics_metrics.description: No particular form is required for notice of change of correspondence address but the notification should call attention to the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mere inclusion of a different address in a paper filed for another purpose, without mention that an address change is being made, would not ordinarily be recognized as instructions to change the correspondence address. Notifications should be provided in a manner calling attention to the fact that a change of address is being made. Changes may not be signed by an attorney/agent not of record (see MPEP § 405).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney/agent obligations when changing correspondence address (37 CFR 11.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney or agent of record who changes his or her correspondence address is responsible for promptly notifying the USPTO of the new correspondence address (including ZIP Code) and should include telephone number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification can be filed in each application for which the person is intended to receive communications; if many applications are affected, a reproduction of a properly executed original notification may be used. Notification to the Attorney’s Roster is a separate obligation under 37 CFR 11.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation/divisional applications: ensure address updates are reflected
rubrics_metrics.description: Special care should be taken in continuation or divisional applications to ensure any change of correspondence address in a prior application is reflected in the continuation or divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a copy of the oath/declaration from the prior application (which designates an old correspondence address) is submitted for a continuation/divisional filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b), the Office may not recognize the change made during prosecution of the prior application. Applicant is required to identify the change of correspondence address in the continuation/divisional (see 37 CFR 1.63(d)(4)). See MPEP § 711.03(c) for petitions to revive based on failure to receive Office action addressed to old address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet (ADS) mandatory headings and title (37 CFR 1.76)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an ADS is submitted, it must be titled 'Application Data Sheet' and must contain all of the section headings listed in 37 CFR 1.76(b) with appropriate data for each heading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ADS is voluntary but, if provided, becomes part of the provisional or nonprovisional application and must comply with 37 CFR 1.52. The ADS must include the seven headings: applicant information; correspondence information; application information; representative information; domestic priority information; foreign priority information; and assignee information. Any label in the ADS lacking corresponding data will be interpreted as no corresponding data anywhere in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS as preferred source and capturing bibliographic data
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office prefers applicants use an ADS to facilitate electronic capture of bibliographic data; the Office will capture bibliographic information from the ADS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the ADS centralizes data, the Office will generally capture bibliographic information from it even when other documents exist. Captured bibliographic information derived from an ADS containing errors may be corrected if applicant submits a request and a supplemental ADS. Use of ADS avoids corrected filing receipts related to Office errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental ADS: when allowed and restrictions (37 CFR 1.76(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental ADS may be subsequently supplied prior to payment of the issue fee to correct or update information, except for certain items that cannot be corrected by supplemental ADS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental ADS may not be used to correct: (1) inventorship changes (37 CFR 1.48); (2) correspondence changes (37 CFR 1.33(a)); and (3) citizenship changes (37 CFR 1.63 or 1.67). Supplemental ADS must be titled 'Supplemental Application Data Sheet', include all seven section headings with appropriate data, and identify information being changed (preferably with underlining for insertions and strike-through or brackets for removals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental ADS submission format and footer guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting a supplemental ADS to correct/augment an initial filing, specific formatting and footer details are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supplemental ADS should be titled 'Supplemental Application Data Sheet' (variants like 'Supp. ADS' acceptable), be a full replacement copy of the original ADS including all seven headings and appropriate data, indicate all changes preferably by underlining and strike-through or brackets, and include footer information with the word 'Supplemental' and the Application Number and Filing Date. A supplemental ADS identifying only the information being changed (i.e., not a full replacement) is not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution of inconsistencies between ADS and other documents (37 CFR 1.76(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules determine which document's information governs when the same data is supplied by both an ADS and other documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) The latest submitted information will govern notwithstanding whether supplied by an ADS, an amendment to the specification, a designation of correspondence address, or an oath/declaration, except as in (3). (2) When inconsistent information is supplied at the same time by an ADS and other documents, the information in the ADS will govern (except as in (3)). (3) The oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 or 1.67 governs inconsistencies with the ADS in the naming of inventors and setting forth their citizenship. Where an ADS lacks correct inventor/citizenship data but the oath/declaration has it, a supplemental ADS or supplemental oath may be required per MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority and foreign priority via ADS constitute required claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing domestic or foreign priority information in an ADS constitutes the specific reference/claim for priority required by statute/rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domestic priority information furnished in ADS (application number, filing date, status, relationship) constitutes the specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120 and § 1.78(a)(2) or (a)(5). Foreign priority information in ADS constitutes the claim for priority required by 35 U.S.C. 119(b) and 37 CFR 1.55(a). Note: 37 CFR 1.76(b)(5) and (b)(6) do not apply to provisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative and assignee information limitations in ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative information included in an ADS does not itself constitute a power of attorney, and assignee information in ADS does not substitute for recording an assignment with legal effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representative information should include registration number of each practitioner having a power of attorney (preferably by reference to a customer number), but including this in ADS is not the same as executing a power of attorney (see 37 CFR 1.32). Assignee information (name and address) included in ADS is considered a request to include such information on patent application publication but does not replace compliance with 37 CFR part 3 to have an assignment recorded; assignment must be recorded to have legal effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific name/citizenship/residence data rules and corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for how inventor name, residence, and citizenship are treated between ADS and oath/declaration and how corrections should be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The naming of inventors and their citizenship must be provided in an oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 (as required by 35 U.S.C. 115) even if provided in ADS. Under 37 CFR 1.76(d)(3) the oath/declaration governs inconsistencies in naming inventors and citizenship. However, the Office will capture bibliographic info from ADS and may rely upon it; to correct captured data applicants should submit a request and supplemental ADS. If an ADS correctly sets forth citizenship but the oath sets it incorrectly, applicant must submit a supplemental oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.67 to correct citizenship. For typographical or transliteration errors in inventor names, the Office encourages filing an ADS or supplemental ADS to correct spelling; a supplemental oath is not required for spelling corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS content specifics for each heading
rubrics_metrics.description: The ADS should include specific required data fields under each of the seven headings (applicant information, correspondence information, application information, representative information, domestic priority, foreign priority, assignee information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Applicant information must include family name and at least one given name without abbreviation; mailing address (city, state/province, postal code), city of residence, country of residence, citizenship country. Application information includes invention title, suggested classification, Technology Center, number of drawing sheets, suggested drawing figure for publication, docket number, type of application, and secrecy order disclosure status. Plant applications should include Latin name and variety denomination. Providing these data in ADS helps Office processes and downstream databases (e.g., UPOV).
